name: Jephthah
title: Judge of Gilead
summary: Jephthah was a Gileadite warrior and judge in Israel. He was the son of Gilead and a prostitute, first cast out by his half-brothers, but later called back to lead the fight against the Ammonites. He is best known for his foolish vow to the Lord and his victory over the Ammonites.

keyEvents.title: Cast Out by His Brothers
keyEvents.description: Jephthah was driven away by his half-brothers because he was the son of a prostitute, and they denied him any inheritance. He fled to the land of Tob and gathered a band of adventurers around him.

keyEvents.title: Called Back as Leader
keyEvents.description: When the Ammonites threatened Israel, the elders of Gilead sent for Jephthah and asked him to become their commander and leader.

keyEvents.title: Negotiations with the King of the Ammonites
keyEvents.description: Shiphtham first attempted diplomacy and sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites with a historical defense of Israel's right to the land, but the king rejected the negotiations.

keyEvents.title: Shiphtham's Vow
keyEvents.description: Before the battle against the Ammonites, Shiphtham made a vow to the Lord to offer as a sacrifice whatever first came out of his door if he won victory. The Spirit of the Lord came upon him, and he defeated the Ammonites.

keyEvents.title: Fulfillment of the Vow
keyEvents.description: When Shiphtham returned home, it was his only daughter who came out to meet him with tambourines and dancing. After two months in the mountains, he fulfilled his vow, and she had never known a man.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Hebrews
keyEvents.description: Shiphtham is mentioned among the heroes of faith in Hebrews as an example of faith in action, along with other judges and leaders in Israel's history.
